applicableAreas: site plan (Sheet 9) - all building setback lines
findings.comment: Required zoning district setback lines (front, rear, interior side, street side) per LDC § 25-2-492 are not shown, labeled, or dimensioned on the site plan. While informal distance dimensions appear from property lines to buildings (19.3', 25', 21.3', 29.6', 46.9', 26.1', 25.8', 33.3'), these are not identified as setback requirement lines with corresponding code citations or identification of required distances. Setback lines must be clearly drawn and labeled with both the required distance and the applicable code section.

Compatibility standards (Article 10) applicability cannot be definitively determined from submitted documents. Site is zoned MF-2 and is adjacent to an SF-3 parcel. New Article 10 (effective July 15, 2024) applies only to sites zoned MF-4 or less restrictive (MF-5, MF-6, commercial, industrial); MF-2 is more restrictive than MF-4 and therefore is not subject to new Article 10. Previous Subchapter F was completely repealed July 15, 2024. Since this plan was submitted May 20, 2025 (after framework change), applicability depends on whether regulatory transition provisions or alternative compatibility frameworks apply to MF-2 sites, which requires City staff clarification.

applicableAreas: electrical transformer pads (Sheet 21) - 4 pads proposed at Bldgs 2, 4/5, 7/8
findings.comment: Transformer pad clearances cannot be verified. Four electrical transformer pads are proposed, but no clearance zones, dimension lines, or building construction type details are provided. Austin Energy Design Criteria 1.10.4 requires different clearances (5 ft for brick/masonry; 12 ft for non-masonry/mixed structures). Building construction types are not specified on the electrical plan, and no clearance radii or measurements are shown, preventing compliance verification.

applicableAreas: wooden fence adjacent to fire hydrant near Bldg 7/8 (Sheet 10)
findings.comment: Fire hydrant fence obstruction accounting cannot be verified. Wooden fence is shown on the Fire Protection Plan adjacent to the private fire hydrant, but fence height is not specified. Per Reviewer Convention, fencing 4 feet or greater in height must be accounted for in hydrant distance measurements. Without a specified height, it cannot be determined whether the fence constitutes an obstruction requiring measurement accommodation.

applicableAreas: wooden privacy fences at property lines (N, E, S boundaries) on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
findings.comment: Solid fence heights cannot be verified. Wooden privacy fences are shown along Northern, Eastern, and Southern property boundaries (designated H-6 in plan legend), but no fence heights are dimensioned or specified anywhere on the plan. LDC § 25-2-899(D) establishes 6-foot maximum height; § 25-2-899(E) permits 7 feet where grade change µ1 foot occurs. Without height dimensions, compliance with applicable maximum standards cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: wooden privacy fences at property lines (N, E, S boundaries) on Landscape Plan (Sheet 31)
findings.comment: Fence design details required by LDC § 25-2-899(I) are not shown on the Landscape Plan. Submittal date May 20, 2025 is after the July 31, 2023 effective date for design restrictions. The code prohibits: spiked pickets above the top horizontal backer rail; vertical pickets with 2-to-9-inch spacing above the top rail; razor wire; barbed wire (except airports); fences creating entrapment/impalement risk; and requires knuckle selvage for solid chain link. The plan must specify fence design and materials demonstrating compliance with these restrictions.
